content.Document: Clinical guideline table of cardiac and extracardiac features / red flags for amyloidosis
Cardiac Findings: Clinical: Hypotension or normotensive if previously hypertensive
ECG: Pseudo-infarct ECG pattern; Low/decreased QRS voltage relative to LV thickness; AV conduction disease
Laboratory: Disproportionately elevated NT-proBNP to degree of HF; Persisting elevated troponin levels

Echocardiography: Granular sparkling of myocardium; Increased right ventricular wall thickness; Increased AV valve thickness; Pericardial effusion; Reduced longitudinal strain with apical sparing pattern
CMR: Subendocardial late gadolinium enhancement (LGE); Elevated native T1 values; Increased extracellular volume; Abnormal gadolinium kinetics
content.Red Flags Table Notes: Table compares findings between TTR and AL amyloidosis (columns labeled 'TTR' and 'AL'); X marks in the table indicate which findings are associated with each type. Examples: Polyneuropathy and dysautonomia are marked for both TTR and AL; macroglossia and skin bruising are marked for AL only; deafness is marked under TTR in the red flag table.

genes.context: Column labeled 'TTR' in the guideline's comparison table of amyloidosis types; X marks under the TTR column indicate association with listed extracardiac red flags (polyneuropathy, dysautonomia, deafness, carpal tunnel, vitreous deposits, family history).
